name: Google Workspace
description: Google Workspace tools for the assistant — Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Gmail, Calendar, Apps Script, Forms, BigQuery and Looker Studio — using your own Google sign-in.
author: Crow

env_vars.name: GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS_FILE
env_vars.description: Path to the OAuth client JSON you downloaded from Google Cloud (client type: Desktop app). Keep it in the same folder as the token file.

env_vars.name: GOOGLE_TOKEN_FILE
env_vars.description: Path where the sign-in token is stored, e.g. ~/.config/google-workspace-mcp/token.json. The folder you choose is the one folder this add-on may write, so the token can be refreshed; run the authorize step once first (see the bundle README).

env_vars.name: GWS_FILES_DIR
env_vars.description: Optional: the one folder this add-on may read and write local files in. Uploads and local-image inserts must name a file inside it; downloads and exports are written into it, and a relative path is relative to it. Anything else is refused, and the Google sign-in folder, ~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg and ~/.config/gcloud are refused whatever you set. Empty (the default) accepts any path but those, unless GWS_OUTBOUND_GUARD is on — then an empty files folder refuses every local file.

env_vars.name: GMAIL_SEND_TO_SELF_ALLOWLIST
env_vars.description: Optional: comma-separated addresses the one sending tool (gmail_send_to_self) may write to. Empty (the default) disables sending — every other Gmail tool only creates drafts.

env_vars.name: GOOGLE_BIGQUERY_PROJECT
env_vars.description: Optional: the Google Cloud project id the BigQuery tools use when a call names none.

env_vars.name: GDOCS_DEFAULT_FONT
env_vars.description: Optional: font applied to text the Docs writing tools insert (e.g. "Arial"). Empty inherits the document's own default.

env_vars.name: GWS_FORMS_SHIM_SCRIPT_ID
env_vars.description: Optional: the Apps Script project id for forms_set_destination's shim (deployment steps in apps-script-shim/). Unset: the tool returns those steps instead of failing.

env_vars.name: GWS_CALENDAR_NO_INVITES
env_vars.description: Optional, off unless set (1/true/on). On: events may only be added to your own calendar — attendees are refused, Google is never asked to email anyone, and responding to an invitation is refused because that emails the organizer.

env_vars.name: GWS_OAUTH_SCOPES
env_vars.description: Optional: the OAuth scopes to authorize and refresh with, instead of the full set — comma- or space-separated short names or full https URLs, e.g. gmail.compose,drive.file,calendar.events. Changing it means re-running the authorize step.

pattern_hint.en: a comma- or space-separated list of scopes, e.g. gmail.compose,drive.file
pattern_hint.es: una lista de permisos separada por comas o espacios, p. ej. gmail.compose,drive.file

env_vars.name: GWS_OUTBOUND_GUARD
env_vars.description: Optional, OFF unless set (1/true/on). On: every action that makes Google send mail or an invitation — calendar guests and invite replies, a Drive share's or ownership transfer's notification email, a Gmail filter's forward address — is refused unless the recipient is on GWS_OUTBOUND_ALLOWLIST. Nothing is sent and no request is made for a refused address.

env_vars.name: GWS_OUTBOUND_ALLOWLIST
env_vars.description: Optional: comma-separated addresses and domains the outbound actions above may reach, e.g. you@example.com,example.org (a domain allows every address at exactly that domain). Read only while GWS_OUTBOUND_GUARD is on; empty then means nothing may be sent.

pattern_hint.en: a comma-separated list of addresses or domains, e.g. you@example.com,example.org
pattern_hint.es: una lista separada por comas de direcciones o dominios, p. ej. tu@example.com,example.org

notes: No ports and no container: a stdio MCP server on this computer, run with uv from the installed copy. Inside the add-on wall it gets the internet (Google's APIs) and exactly one folder of yours, read-write — the folder holding the token file, because the OAuth token is rewritten there when it refreshes; name a files folder (GWS_FILES_DIR) and it gets that one too, read-write, and every local path a tool takes must land inside it. Point both GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS_FILE and GOOGLE_TOKEN_FILE at ~/.config/google-workspace-mcp/ and it finds both. Sending mail is off until GMAIL_SEND_TO_SELF_ALLOWLIST names your own address; everything else drafts. The actions that make Google write to someone else (calendar guests, invite replies, share notifications, ownership transfers, Gmail filter forwards) are sorted out before they leave: GWS_CALENDAR_NO_INVITES drops invitations entirely, and GWS_OUTBOUND_GUARD (off by default) refuses any recipient not on GWS_OUTBOUND_ALLOWLIST. The tools that take a LOCAL path (drive upload/download/export, slides export, a local image for a doc) never touch the sign-in folder, ~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg or ~/.config/gcloud, whatever else is set.
